name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)

field_reviews.reason: Fetched developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/get-started/authentication/ directly: third-party integrations use OAuth 1.0a with HMAC-signed requests (consumer key/secret + access token generated on integration activation), which is the documented path for external integrations; token-based bearer auth is positioned for mobile/registered-user clients.

bearer_token (admin/customer token services) and hmac_signature (OAuth 1.0a integrations) are directly confirmed on the live authentication page. oauth2_authorization_code applies only to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service via Adobe IMS, where the page points primarily to a server-to-server integration guide (client-credentials style) alongside a user IMS-token guide; the core Magento Open Source / PaaS platform has no OAuth 2.0 at all. The entry is defensible for SaaS user flows but is the weakest of the three.

Magento Open Source is free and self-hostable, and the authentication docs confirm store admins mint tokens/integrations themselves (System > Extensions > Integration); no vendor gate for OSS. Adobe Commerce being enterprise-sales is correctly relegated to notes.

Value is correct - the REST API reference documents 'all available REST API endpoints in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source' spanning admin, customer and guest operations (catalog, orders, customers, inventory, carts), plus a full GraphQL schema - but the draft carried no evidence URL for the api claim, so replacement evidence was found.

Value is correct but the draft had no evidence URL for it. The official getting-started page confirms 'Support for GraphQL, REST (Representational State Transfer) and SOAP' across Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source; SOAP also exists but is legacy and outside the protocol enum, as the draft's uncertainty notes already acknowledged.

Two-part claim re-verified. (1) The npm package @adobe-commerce/commerce-extensibility-tools exists (latest 3.5.0, Apache-2.0, 'mcp' keyword, maintainers with adobe.com emails - ownership verified via registry.npmjs.org), a shipped official vendor MCP for App Builder extensibility development. (2) The flagship Commerce MCP was announced at Adobe Summit (business.adobe.com blog, 2026-04-20) but the Experience League overview page (fetched live, updated June 17 2026) still carries a 'Coming Soon' badge - exactly as the draft's notes disclosed. official_vendor_mcp stands on the shipped npm server.
Free self-hosted Open Source plus self-serve admin tokens/integrations means an integration is buildable today against any store whose admin cooperates.
No vendor-side gate for the open-source platform; the per-store admin requirement is inherent to self-hosted software, not an access blocker.

notes: Main assignment was finding real evidence for the api claim that shipped without a URL: confirmed REST+GraphQL (and legacy SOAP) at developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/get-started/ and the full REST reference at /commerce/webapi/rest/reference/ - PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED with replacement evidence rather than contradiction, since the draft values were correct. Also fetched the draft's authentication evidence URL live (exists, matches) and re-verified both MCP claims including npm package ownership (adobe.com maintainer emails) and the 'Coming Soon' status of the Summit-announced Commerce MCP.
